messages.author: 1350af9e0cd5ed64
messages.subject: Multiple group CFA. Error: arguments imply differing number of rows error
parts:
Hi guys,

I'm trying to run a multiple-group CFA on an imputated dataset (m=25) created in Amelia II

Here's my model:

model<-'
Factor1=~Q437+Q439+Q441
Factor2=~Q445+Q447+Q449+Q451+Q453
'
Multigroup CFA:

config<-runMI(model, data=data$imputations, chi="mplus",fun="cfa", group = "Gender")
weak<-runMI(model, data=data$imputations, chi = "mplus", fun="cfa",group= "Gender", group.equal = "loadings")
strong <- runMI(model, data=data$imputations, chi = "mplus", fun="cfa", group="Gender", group.equal=c("loadings","intercepts"))
strict <- runMI(model, data=data$imputations, chi = "mplus", fun="cfa", group="Gender", group.equal=c("loadings","intercepts","residuals"))

config runs perfectly, but weak, strong and strict give off errors such as:
Error in data.frame(..., check.names = FALSE) : 
  arguments imply differing number of rows: 58, 64

Adding group.equal="loadings" is enough to break config and give this error.

can anyone see what I've done wrong here? I've tried using older versions of lavaan, R and SemTools the error is the same for each of them.

R version: 3.2.0
lavaan: 0.5-18
SemTools: 0.4-6
Amelia II: 1.7.3

Thanks,

James

> I tried this with multiple versions of R, and spoke to a few other users

> lavaan. The results I got back above were actually impossible even
> though I managed to get lavaan to give me back something. I'll try and
> get a replicatable example together and submit a bug report.

As soon as I can replicate it, I will fix it. But note that runMI() is a
function of the package semTools, not lavaan!

Wild guess: runMI needs the package Amelia, which in turn requires Rcpp.
I noticed that the latter package changes a lot, and often needs to be
reinstalled.

So what I would suggest is:

- (re)install Rcpp
- (re)install RcppArmadillo
- (re)install Amelia
- (re)install semTools

Then,

- start a fresh session of R, outside Rstudio
- remove the workspace: rm(list=ls()) (to avoid confusion with stored
objects in your workspace)
- load the lavaan + semTools packages (only)

and try again.

Keep us posted.

Yves.

parts:
I'll try to simulate some data to replicate the results. Thus far, this is what I've identified related to this issue:

My syntax runs when R=3.1.2, Amelia=1.7.3, Rcpp=0.11.5, RcppArmadillo=0.4.650.1.1, lavaan=0.5-17, and semTools=0.4-6
My syntax does not run when R=3.2.0, Amelia=1.7.3, Rcpp=0.11.6, RcppArmadillo=0.5.200.1.0, lavaan=0.5-18, and semTools=0.4-6

When equal.group=NULL, it runs regardless of setup but as soon as something is entered there, I get the different number of rows error.

I ran the code with verbose=T, and realized that when it works (either because of the 3.1.2 setup or because of no cross-group equivalencies), it runs through the optimizer 2*#imputed datasets (first set takes more iterations to converge than second set), but when it does not run, it errors out after 1*#imputed --- I don't know enough about the inner workings of runMI, but my hunch is that the first #imputed is fitting the model, whereas the second set is fitting the null model? If that's the case, the error is somewhere between those two steps.

Aaron

messages.subject: Re: Multiple group CFA. Error: arguments imply differing number of rows error
parts:
Hmmmm. My guess is that the issue is with the computation of the Mplus (or mr) chi-square statistic. For those statistics we need to fit multiple models to each imputed dataset (the target model, the null model, a saturated model, and models with all parameters fixed). Anecdotally, computing the saturated model/model with all fixed parameters is where things get wonky. To see if this is the issue, try to run your code with the chi argument set to either "none" or "lmrr".

A reproducible example would be great to help debug any issues.

Alex

messages.author: af82fa98896529e2
messages.subject: Re: Multiple group CFA. Error: arguments imply differing number of rows error
parts:
I have fixed the issue. Download the following package:

https://github.com/simsem/semTools/raw/master/builds/semTools_0.4-9.tar.gz 

Then, use the following command to install the package:

install.packages("semTools_0.4-9.tar.gz", repos = NULL, type = "source")

The issue is from labeling the pooled coefficients. It was my carelessness that did not check runMI when equality constraints exist this time.
